validity.recommendation: No action needed on core identity/specs; existence, classification, ownership, length, diameter, capacity, fuel source and proposal year are all well corroborated by independent sources. See separate attribution and spec concerns below.
validity.researcher_notes: TAPI is a real, extensively documented cross-border megaproject (four intergovernmental signatories, a dedicated project company TAPI Pipeline Company Ltd/TPCL incorporated Nov 2014, decades of trade-press and multilateral-lender coverage through 2026) -- no existence doubt. Classification (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission) is trivially correct for a 56in trunk line moving field gas 1,814 km to four countries. No duplicate risk against the 26-row India-gas roster -- nothing else resembles a cross-border TAPI leg. Confirmed against >=2 independent sources: (1) Length 1,814 km -- offshore-technology.com ('1,814km trans-country natural gas pipeline') + en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India_Pipeline (contains '1,814'). (2) Diameter 56in -- same two sources (offshore-technology.com states '56in'; Wikipedia page contains '56'). (3) Capacity 33 bcm/y -- offshore-technology.com ('33 billion cubic meters of gas a year'), corroborated further by jamestown.org, worldpipelines.com (12/06/2023 article) and theprint.in, all of which contain '33 billion' in the same context -- four independent hits, high tier. (4) FuelSource = Galkynysh Gas Field -- offshore-technology.com TAPI project page + en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galkynysh_Gas_Field both name it as the source field (the historical-alias parenthetical 'Iolotan/South Yolotan-Osman' is a widely reported prior name for the same field but I could not independently verify that exact alias text on the Galkynysh Wikipedia page as currently phrased -- low-priority naming footnote, not a data error). (5) ProposalYear 2010 -- nsenergybusiness.com ('The four countries signed an Inter Government Agreement (IGA) and Gas Pipeline Framework Agreements (GPFA) in December 2010') and offshore-technology.com ('An inter-governmental agreement (IGA) was signed in 2010... A Gas Pipeline Framework Agreement (GPFA) was also signed... in December 2010') -- two independent sources agree the 2010 IGA/GPFA is the correct proposal-year anchor. (6) Owners Turkmengaz 85% / Afghan Gas Enterprise 5% / Interstate Gas Systems 5% / GAIL (India) Ltd 5% -- offshore-technology.com and interfax.com (2026 Kazakhstan-stake story, which restates the current cap table) both give the identical 85/5/5/5 split; note Kazakhstan has publicly sought a 30% stake as of 2025-2026 but that is a live negotiation, not an executed change -- do not alter Owner% on this alone, worth re-checking at next sweep. (7) ConstructionYear/Month 2024-09 and Status=construction remain correct and current -- see status_reviews below. EndLocation Fazilka / EndState Punjab / EndCountryOrArea India confirmed by offshore-technology.com ('terminates in Fazilka at the Indo-Pakistan border in Punjab region, India') and Wikipedia (contains 'Fazilka').

validity.recommendation: Change StartState/Province from 'Ahal' to 'Mary' (Mary Region/Velayat, Turkmenistan). Optionally add StartLocation once a specific town/facility is confirmed (candidates seen in sourcing: the Galkynysh field itself, or Serhetabat, the Turkmen border town ~75km from the field where the pipeline crosses into Afghanistan -- I did not stage a value here because sources use these two distinct reference points interchangeably and I don't want to fabricate false precision).
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's StartState/Province for this row is 'Ahal', but every independent source I could find places the pipeline's Turkmenistan starting point in Mary Region, not Ahal. The source gas field, Galkynysh, is itself located in Mary Province (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galkynysh_Gas_Field: 'located in Mary Province... near Yoloten'; offshore-technology.com's own Galkynysh field page independently states the same). The TAPI project page (offshore-technology.com) states the pipeline 'begins from Mary region of Turkmenistan.' A broader web search for any TAPI source mentioning 'Ahal' in connection with the pipeline's starting point returned nothing -- multiple sources instead describe construction starting at Serhetabat, a Turkmen town in Mary Region on the Afghan border (~75km from the Galkynysh field). I found no source anywhere that supports Ahal as the correct province. This looks like a genuine data-entry error, not a difference-of-opinion or a legitimate alternate framing -- three independent sources (Wikipedia's Galkynysh Gas Field article, offshore-technology.com's Galkynysh Gas Field project page, and offshore-technology.com's separate TAPI project page) all converge on Mary.

validity.recommendation: Add SegmentCostYear=2018 to date the existing $7bn SegmentCost figure, and flag for re-verification closer to any FID announcement -- do not treat $7bn as a durable current estimate. Consider noting the $10bn figure (the more commonly cited industry-database estimate, e.g. offshore-technology.com's project page) as a documented alternate in ResearcherNotes.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's SegmentCost of $7,000,000,000 USD traces to a real, specific, dateable statement: in November 2018 TAPI Pipeline Company CEO Muhammetmyrat Amanov told an industry conference in Abu Dhabi that the project's cost had been cut ~30% from an original $10bn estimate to about $7bn (with a first-stage cost of ~$5bn). I verified this exact figure on two outlets -- dawn.com/news/1445485 and business-standard.com/article/reuters/tapi-pipeline-ceo-says-first-gas-to-pakistan-in-around-two-years-118111301159_1.html -- but both are visibly the same Reuters wire story ('UPDATE 1-Tapi gas pipeline to move forward after decades of delays', Reuters, Nov. 13 2018, also cited on gem.wiki itself) republished by two outlets, which per the corroboration rule counts as ONE source, not two independent ones. Separately, cost estimates for this project have varied widely across time and source: $10bn is the figure most commonly given by industry-database pages describing the project in general terms (offshore-technology.com's TAPI page currently states '$10bn'), and other secondary compilations cite figures from $4-5bn up to $7.6bn and $8bn at various points. Given (a) the $7bn figure is a single-wire-origin quote now 7+ years old, (b) it was explicitly framed even at the time as an aspirational cost-cut target tied to a since-repeatedly-slipped FID, and (c) more recent describe-the-project sources default to $10bn, I'm flagging this as a spec concern rather than silently endorsing $7bn as current. I am not proposing to overwrite the value outright since it IS a real, sourceable historical figure -- just recommending it be dated and re-checked.

fills.researcher_notes: Both sources independently date the intergovernmental agreement (IGA) and Gas Pipeline Framework Agreement (GPFA) among Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan and India to December 2010 -- the correct anchor for ProposalYear=2010.
33 bcm/y (33 billion cubic meters a year) is confirmed verbatim by three independent outlets spanning 2023-2025 coverage.

1,814 km total length confirmed by two independent sources; also echoed in the sheet's own cited IJGlobal transaction title, though the IJGlobal page itself is behind a data-paywall and failed url_verifier so I did not cite it.
56in diameter confirmed verbatim by two independent sources.

Both proposed refs are the same Reuters wire story (Nov 13, 2018) republished by two outlets -- NOT independent per the corroboration rule, hence class_out=UNRESOLVED despite having verified URLs. Dating the value to SegmentCostYear=2018 is the useful fix here; see the paired validity spec-concern entry for the full caveat about staleness vs. the more commonly cited $10bn figure.

The 85% / 5% / 5% / 5% split across Turkmengaz, Afghan Gas Enterprise (interfax.com uses 'Afghan Gas Corporation', a minor naming variant for the same entity), Interstate Gas Systems and GAIL (India) Ltd is confirmed verbatim by two independent, differently-dated sources (the project profile page and a 2026 Kazakhstan-stake news story that restates the current cap table). Note: Kazakhstan has publicly sought a 30% stake in TAPI as of 2025-2026 (interfax.com) but this is an unresolved negotiation, not an executed ownership change -- do not alter Owner% on this basis; worth re-checking at the next sweep.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is a cross-border row (TAPI), so per the country-specific guidance PNGRB's domestic register does not cover it -- judged on sponsor/national sources instead. Status=construction (set 2025-08-21, ConstructionYear/Month=2024-09 per the existing, already-verified worldpipelines.com Sept-2024 ref) is well supported by newer, independent evidence: Pajhwok Afghan News (2026-05-20, '64km of TAPI pipeline laid in Afghanistan'), Ariana News (2026-06-15, 'around 84 kilometres of pipeline have now been installed... approximately 60 percent complete'), and Kabul Tribune ('52% of TAPI Pipeline Work Completed in Herat'). All three are independent Afghan outlets reporting active, ongoing physical construction on the Afghan section as of May-June 2026, consistent with progressive month-over-month progress figures (64km -> 84km). This is unambiguously an active-construction project, not dormant -- no dormancy/staleness rule applies. Delayed=yes / DelayType=confirmed also still holds (project has slipped repeatedly against every prior FID/completion target since the 2010 IGA) and needs no change.

summary: TAPI (P0766): existence/classification/ownership/length/diameter/capacity/fuel-source/proposal-year all confirmed by 2+ independent sources and status=construction reconfirmed current (Afghan-section progress reported through June 2026, ~60% of the Afghan leg complete); flagged one attribution error (StartState/Province='Ahal' should be 'Mary', the Galkynysh field's actual province -- 3 independent sources, no source supports Ahal) and one spec caveat (SegmentCost=$7bn traces to a single 2018 Reuters wire quote, now dated, vs. the more commonly cited $10bn figure -- recommend dating it SegmentCostYear=2018 and re-checking near FID).
